title: Open May by Sorting the Loose Ends
teaser: Carrying every unfinished task into a new month can create weight without creating value.
full_text: Sort April's open items into three groups today: finish, postpone, and release. Put only the work you truly intend to carry into May on the new plan.

title: Search for Evidence Against Your Decision
teaser: Looking only for support can make a weak assumption feel stronger than it is.
full_text: For one important decision, write what evidence would make you change your mind. Look for that evidence before treating the choice as settled.

title: Find the First Point Where a Repeated Problem Breaks
teaser: Fixing the final symptom again and again can hide the actual source of failure.
full_text: Trace one recurring problem backward through its steps. Identify the earliest point where reality first departed from what the process expected.

title: Ask a Narrower Question
teaser: Questions that are too broad often produce answers that are difficult to use.
full_text: When you need information today, narrow one question around a single topic, date, or decision. Notice whether the more precise question produces a more actionable answer.

title: Put a Waiting Period on a Nonessential Purchase
teaser: Time can reveal the difference between an immediate urge and a durable need.
full_text: Delay one nonessential purchase for a short, defined period. At the end, check whether the need, price, and effect on your budget still make sense.

title: Make the Start of a Good Habit Easier
teaser: Reducing the friction of beginning can make consistency more realistic.
full_text: Prepare the first step of one habit you want to keep. Place the needed item where you can see it or remove one decision that normally delays the start.

title: Save the Date Along With the Claim
teaser: Even accurate information can become outdated when its context changes.
full_text: Add the source date to one important fact you are saving today. Make it easy for future-you to check whether the information is still current before relying on it.

title: Name the Final Owner of Shared Work
teaser: When everyone is responsible, an important task can still end up with no clear owner.
full_text: For one collaborative task, name who is accountable for following the result through. Keep contributors and final ownership distinct.

title: Give Your Priority a Real Place on the Calendar
teaser: A task can sit at the top of a list and still receive no actual time.
full_text: Reserve a realistic block today for the work you call most important. Choose a startable window rather than an idealized amount of time you rarely have.

title: Name a File for the Person Searching Later
teaser: Vague filenames quietly create search work for the future.
full_text: Rename or create one important file with a useful topic, date, or version marker. Avoid names such as 'final2' that lose meaning once the moment has passed.

title: Do Not Guess Someone Else's Boundary
teaser: Good intentions do not automatically tell you what another person is comfortable with.
full_text: In one situation involving someone close to you, ask what is acceptable instead of assuming. Take the answer as given rather than translating it into what you hoped to hear.

title: Identify the Most Fragile Dependency in a Plan
teaser: A plan can be only as reliable as the outside condition it depends on most.
full_text: Choose one important plan and identify the external condition that must hold for it to work. Write a fallback for delay or failure before you need it.

title: Count Interruptions During One Work Block
teaser: A vague feeling of distraction does not always reveal what should change.
full_text: During one defined work block today, count unplanned interruptions. At the end, choose one practical response to the source that appeared most often.

title: Do Not Turn a Body Signal Into a Performance Contest
teaser: Ignoring a real need for recovery can trade short-term output for a harder reset later.
full_text: If you notice marked fatigue, pain, or exhaustion today, do not automatically push the pace higher. Take rest seriously and seek appropriate professional advice when symptoms warrant it.

title: Record What You Chose Not to Do
teaser: A deliberate omission can reveal as much about planning quality as a completed task.
full_text: Write down one item you intentionally removed from May and why. At month-end, check whether that decision actually created useful space.

title: Track a Skill by Deliberate Repetitions
teaser: Early outcomes can be noisy while repeated practice gives a clearer view of effort.
full_text: For one skill you are building, record the number of focused repetitions as well as the result. Decide on the next small practice session.

title: Pair a No With a Clear Alternative When Appropriate
teaser: Setting a boundary does not always require shutting down the conversation.
full_text: If you cannot accept a request today, give a concise no instead of vague delay. When it is genuinely possible, offer a realistic later time or narrower scope.

title: Inspect the Scale of a Chart
teaser: The same data can look dramatic or trivial depending on how an axis is drawn.
full_text: Check the axis start, interval, and unit on one chart influencing a decision today. Ask whether the visual impression is larger than the numerical difference.

title: Define Acceptance Before You Deliver
teaser: The word 'done' can mean different things to different people.
full_text: Before finishing one deliverable, write two or three concrete conditions that make it acceptable. Use those conditions during the final review.

title: Verify That a Backup Can Be Read
teaser: The existence of a backup file does not prove that recovery will work.
full_text: For one important digital backup, confirm more than its presence. Where safe, verify that it can be opened or that the documented restore steps still work.

title: Describe the Behavior Instead of Labeling the Person
teaser: Broad character labels often increase defensiveness without improving the situation.
full_text: When discussing a problem today, describe the observable behavior and its effect. Keep the requested change concrete instead of turning it into a judgment about personality.

title: Try Checking Nonurgent Notifications in Batches
teaser: Frequent small checking loops can fragment deeper attention.
full_text: Choose one or two times to review nonurgent messages and notifications today. Between those times, notice the impulse to reopen apps without a real need.

title: Define a Project by the Change It Should Produce
teaser: A project list can grow while the intended outcome becomes less clear.
full_text: For one active project, answer this in one sentence: what will be different when this is finished? Judge the next tasks against that sentence.

title: Ask About the Cost of Reversing a Choice
teaser: Some decisions are easy to change while others make reversal expensive.
full_text: When comparing two options today, note which one is easier to undo. Under high uncertainty, include reversibility as part of the decision rather than ignoring it.

title: Keep a Second Copy of Something Critical
teaser: A single copy is fragile when hardware, access, or accidental deletion fails.
full_text: Confirm that one document or dataset whose loss would matter has a current second copy. Consider whether storing both copies on the same device leaves the same risk intact.

title: Separate Expected Income From Usable Cash
teaser: Money you expect and money available to spend may not arrive at the same time.
full_text: For one income item in your budget, distinguish the expected date from the date the funds are realistically usable. Avoid scheduling obligations only against the optimistic date.

title: Add a Delay to an Unwanted Habit
teaser: Slowing an automatic response can sometimes be more workable than demanding an instant permanent ban.
full_text: Add a five- or ten-minute delay before one behavior you want to reduce. During the pause, observe whether the trigger remains as strong as it first felt.

title: Add a Real Example to a Learning Note
teaser: An abstract rule can survive in memory while the context for using it disappears.
full_text: Take one concept you learned and add a short example from your work or daily life. Make the moment of application visible, not only the definition.

title: Count Open Loops and Give Each a Status
teaser: Small unfinished matters can occupy attention without appearing important on their own.
full_text: List open tasks, awaited replies, and unresolved decisions today. Do not force yourself to finish everything; give each one a clear next status.

title: Choose One Priority to Carry Into June
teaser: Moving everything forward can fill a new month with old weight before it starts.
full_text: Select the one May priority that genuinely deserves to move into June. For the rest, decide whether to finish, postpone deliberately, or remove them.

title: Close May With Evidence
teaser: A month reviewed only by feeling can make progress and problems look different from what actually happened.
full_text: Choose three concrete pieces of evidence from May: one completed result, one changed measure, and one lesson. Use those facts to shape June.
